thought_title: Welcome the bishop as the Sender

edition.witness_note: Lake 1912 Loeb copy-text; Lightfoot/Funk middle recension not yet locked as second witness

source_text: [1] Καὶ ὅσον βλέπει τις σιγῶντα ἐπίσκοπον, πλειόνως αὐτὸν φοβείσθω: πάντα γάρ, ὃν πέμπει ὁ οἰκοδεσπότης εἰς ἰδίαν οἰκονομίαν, οὕτως δεῖ ἡμᾶς αὐτὸν δέχεσθαι, ὡς αὐτὸν τὸν πέμψαντα, τὸν οὖν ἐπίσκοπον δῆλον ὅτι ὡς αὐτὸν κύριον δεῖ προσβλέπειν. [2] αὐτὸς μὲν οὖν Ὀνήσιμος ὑπερεπαινεῖ ὑμῶν τὴν ἐν θεῷ εὐταξίαν, ὅτι πάντες κατὰ ἀλήθειαν ζῆτε καὶ ὅτι ἐν ὑμῖν οὐδεμία αἵρεσις κατοικεῖ: ἀλλ’ οὐδὲ ἀκούετέ τινος πλέον, ἢ περὶ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ λαλοῦντος ἐν ἀληθείᾳ.
pass_a_gloss: And the more anyone sees a bishop keeping silent, the more let him fear him. For everyone whom the master of the house sends to manage his own household, we must receive in the same way as the one who sent him. So it is clear that we must look on the bishop as the Lord himself. Now Onesimus himself highly praises your good order in God: that you all live according to the truth, and that no faction has a home among you; in fact you do not even listen to anyone beyond one who speaks truthfully about Jesus Christ.
pass_b_english: The more anyone sees a bishop keeping silent, the more let him stand in awe of him. Whoever the Master of the house sends to run his household, we must welcome as we would welcome the one who sent him (Matthew 10:40; John 13:20). Plainly, then, we must regard the bishop as the Lord himself.

Onesimus himself warmly praises your good order in God. You all live by the truth, and no faction makes its home among you. In fact, you do not even listen to anyone more than to one who speaks truly about Jesus Christ.

choices.term: ὅσον βλέπει τις σιγῶντα ἐπίσκοπον, πλειόνως αὐτὸν φοβείσθω
choices.english: The more anyone sees a bishop keeping silent, the more let him stand in awe of him
choices.why: φοβέομαι here is reverent fear; Ignatius defends a quiet bishop against those who despise his silence.
In Ignatius αἵρεσις is still a party or split; 'heresy' imports a later technical sense.

choices.term: οὐδὲ ἀκούετέ τινος πλέον, ἢ περὶ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ λαλοῦντος ἐν ἀληθείᾳ
choices.english: you do not even listen to anyone more than to one who speaks truly about Jesus Christ
choices.why: περί + genitive makes Jesus Christ the subject matter of the speaker, not the speaker.
rejected: rather than to Jesus Christ speaking in truth (ANF; misreads περί)

anf_compare.notes: ANF ends 'Nor do you hearken to any one rather than to Jesus Christ speaking in truth', making Christ the speaker. The Greek τινος ... περὶ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ λαλοῦντος means a person speaking about Jesus Christ. ANF 'to be over His household' and 'no sect' are otherwise close.

bible_refs.note: ὁ δεχόμενος ... δέχεται τὸν ἀποστείλαντά με: receiving the one sent as the sender
receiving whomever I send receives the one who sent me (τὸν πέμψαντά με)

notes: Whole chapter 6 (sections 1-2) matches the ANF span.
ANF marks Matthew 24:45 (the household steward); the οἰκοδεσπότης image fits Gospel parables generally but no single verse matches. Not inline.

review.notes: p1 checked in full. Greek 'ὅσον βλέπει τις σιγῶντα ἐπίσκοπον, πλειόνως αὐτὸν φοβείσθω' matches A 'the more anyone sees a bishop keeping silent, the more let him fear him' and B 'stand in awe' (reverent φοβέομαι, not a reversal). 'πάντα γάρ, ὃν πέμπει ὁ οἰκοδεσπότης εἰς ἰδίαν οἰκονομίαν ... ὡς αὐτὸν τὸν πέμψαντα' and 'ὡς αὐτὸν κύριον δεῖ προσβλέπειν' are kept: receive the one sent as the sender; regard the bishop as the Lord himself. Onesimus (αὐτὸς ... Ὀνήσιμος ὑπερεπαινεῖ) remains the praiser of 'τὴν ἐν θεῷ εὐταξίαν'; both negations hold ('οὐδεμία αἵρεσις κατοικεῖ'; 'οὐδὲ ἀκούετέ τινος πλέον'). περί is not flipped: A 'speaks truthfully about Jesus Christ' and B 'speaks truly about Jesus Christ' make Christ the subject matter. B's '(Matthew 10:40; John 13:20)' sits on the reception clause, consistent with the supplied wording notes, not the steward image. Title names the reception thought.
